record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two that contains at least one non-special function. Is S left reversible if and only if any two elements of S have a common iterate? Here left reversible means that for every A, B in S there exist X, Y in S such that A∘X = B∘Y.

evidence.quote: We recall that a semigroup S is called left reversible if for all A, B in S there exist X, Y in S such that (1) AX = BY.

Conjecture 4.3. Let S be a semigroup of rational functions of degree at least two containing at least one non-special function. Then S is left reversible if and only if any two elements of S have a common iterate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a semigroup, under composition, of rational functions of degree at least two on the Riemann sphere $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}=\mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$. A rational function of degree at least two is called special if it is either conjugate (by a Möbius transformation) to a power map $z\mapsto z^{\pm n}$, to a Chebyshev polynomial $\pm T_n(z)$, or to a Lattès map (a map induced by an endomorphism of an elliptic curve). The semigroup $S$ is called left reversible if for every $A,B\in S$ there exist $X,Y\in S$ such that $A\circ X = B\circ Y$. Two elements $A,B\in S$ are said to have a common iterate if there exist positive integers $m,n$ with $A^{\circ m}=B^{\circ n}$, where $A^{\circ k}$ denotes the $k$-fold composition of $A$ with itself.

Assume that $S$ contains at least one non-special rational function. Prove or disprove: $S$ is left reversible if and only if every two elements of $S$ have a common iterate.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture about semigroups of rational functions containing at least one non-special element. No published resolution (positive or negative) was found in the literature; related results by Pakovich concern amenability and commuting/semiconjugate rational functions, but the equivalence between left reversibility and the existence of common iterates for such semigroups appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses left/right reversibility of semigroups of rational functions and related power-joined and common-iterate properties.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture appears in the same line of research on reversibility of rational-function semigroups, with no resolution found.

status_evidence.title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems and conjectures including the equivalence between left reversibility and common iterates for non-special semigroups.
